data.title: Ameriprise Financial 3Q 2026: Revenue $5.19B, Net income $1.13B, EPS $12.32— 10-Q Summary
data.description:
Ameriprise Financial reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $5.19 billion, up 6.1% from a year earlier, while net income rose 23.5% to $1.13 billion and diluted EPS increased 32% to $12.32.

Financial Highlights

  • Revenue was $5.19B, compared with $4.89B in the prior-year quarter; YoY change 6.1%.
  • Net income was $1.13B, compared with $912M in the prior-year quarter; YoY change 23.5%.
  • Diluted EPS was $12.32, compared with $9.33 in the prior-year quarter; YoY change 32%.

Business Highlights

  • Advice & Wealth adjusted earnings rose 16% year to date, supported by market gains, client inflows and advisor productivity. Advisory wrap assets increased 18% year over year, with nine-month net inflows of $17.8B.
  • Asset Management adjusted earnings increased 18% year to date, aided by equity markets and strong Seligman technology strategies despite net outflows.
  • Retirement & Protection adjusted earnings fell 19% year to date, reflecting assumption updates, annuity outflows and higher sales-related costs.
  • Ameriprise continues to recruit experienced advisors and expects the shift toward lower-risk products and away from variable annuity living-benefit guarantees to continue.

Original SEC Filing: AMERIPRISE FINANCIAL INC [ AMP ] - 10-Q - Oct. 30, 2026

data.title: Nvidia Stock Is Set for Its Worst Month in a Year. Time to Buy the Dip. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Jack Denton

There's nothing like stock market carnage to clarify genuine investor optimism.

Nvidia stock tumbled 3% Friday, falling along with other chipmakers as the wider tech sector sold off.

Chip stocks have had a rough go amid worries over debt and the sustainability of artificial-intelligence spending. The latest declines were triggered by earnings from Amazon.com and Intel, both of which spooked investors over cash flow concerns.

For Nvidia investors, this might be the time to buy the dip. Nvidia stock is trading at its lowest levels since early August and, if early action on Friday is anything to go by, is set to close out October with a decline of more than 9%. That would mark the worst month since November 2025, when it fell 12.6%. Nvidia stock is on track for its worst performance in the first 10 months of a year since 2022, up just 11% in 2026 so far.

The fact remains that, if investors liked Nvidia a month ago, they should still like it today. Wall Street certainly agrees. Despite its drop over the last month, 96% of analysts surveyed by FactSet rated Nvidia stock a Buy, with an average target price of $334, which implies the shares could climb more than 60% from their current level.

Barron's has previously reported that the chip stock chaos is likely to, above all else, sort the winners from the losers. No matter the pinch Nvidia stock has felt in recent weeks — and no matter that debt and AI spending are significant considerations — the chipmaker remains at the top of the AI game.

Write to Jack Denton at jack.denton@barrons.com

data.title: Fuel trader Atlas Oil accused in US court filing of mixing cyanide-releasing compound into gasoline
data.description:
Key points:
  • Modern Chemical alleges Atlas blended gasoline with 15% to 20% propionitrile in shipments to Mexico
  • Petition alleges blended fuel appears to have contributed to death of 34-year-old railcar worker
  • Atlas lawyers call Modern's allegations and racketeering claims without foundation

By Arathy Somasekhar

A chemical company has accused Houston-based fuel trader Atlas Oil Company of mixing a toxic, cyanide-releasing compound into gasoline and said in a court filing this month that the fuel appears to have contributed to a worker's death.

Modern Chemical, also known as Commercial Beverage Concepts, alleged in the filing in the Texas Business Court that Atlas secretly mixed propionitrile, a deadly compound that releases cyanide and is not an approved fuel additive, into gasoline.

The allegations, made in a counter petition in a commercial dispute over unpaid fuel shipments to Mexico, accuse Atlas of breaking federal transport rules and violating the Clean Air Act. Modern also alleges that Atlas engaged in a pattern of racketeering activity, including committing bank fraud and money laundering.

The court filing also ties the blended fuel to the death of a worker in Aransas Pass, Texas, whose family is suing Atlas and two other companies separately.

The allegations raise questions about fuel safety, compliance with federal transportation and environmental regulations, and whether the disputed fuel contributed to the death of a Texas railcar worker. Atlas, which has said the allegations are without foundation, plans to seek a dismissal, while the worker's family is pursuing a separate negligence lawsuit.

MODERN'S ALLEGATIONS DETAILED

Modern alleges that Atlas would blend 80% to 85% gasoline with 15% to 20% propionitrile despite knowing as early as May 2, 2025, that the compound was not approved for use as a fuel additive, and that it was a toxic substance that, if inhaled, ingested or absorbed through the skin, could kill a person even in low concentrations.

Companies often blend lower-cost materials into fuel to improve margins, according to traders and people in the industry. Propionitrile, however, is not on the US Environmental Protection Agency's list of approved gasoline additives, according to Modern's petition.

"Atlas’s fraudulent conduct ... violated several criminal statutes and appears to have actually killed a thirty-four year old father working at a railcar transload facility who was splashed with some of the blended fuel and died two days later," the petition alleged, citing a report from the US Occupational Safety and Health Administration and an obituary for Felix Fonseca Jr.

Atlas' lawyers at Baker McKenzie said in a statement to Reuters that Modern's allegations, including its racketeering claims, are without foundation.

"Atlas intends to respond in full in due course with a motion to dismiss and to seek recovery of fees," the lawyers said. "Because this is pending litigation, Atlas will not comment further on the specific allegations at this time."

COMPANIES DISPUTE FUEL TESTING PRACTICES

Modern in its petition has alleged that Atlas transported the adulterated fuel using false placards on the railcars in violation of several federal statutes and regulations.

Modern has also alleged that when Atlas learned that certain fuel tests could detect the blended substance, Atlas directed its vendor to test the blend differently, with an apparent goal of diluting the sample to mask the presence of the compound.

Such blending also violates the Clean Air Act, as propionitrile is not a permissible additive for motor vehicle gasoline, the petition alleges.

All product Atlas sold to Modern was certified through a reputable railcar inspection service in the United States prior to shipment, Atlas said in a filing, while alleging that Modern engaged in "improper, unreliable testing" of the product in Mexico.

Modern did not respond to a request for additional comments.

data.title: Major European Markets End Mixed As Investors React To Earnings, Economic Data
data.description:
BRUSSELS/FRANKFURT/PARIS (dpa-AFX) - The major European markets closed mixed on Friday even as most of the other markets across the continent ended notably lower, as investors reacted to a slew of corporate earnings announcements and the latest batch of regional economic data.

Higher oil prices and weakness in the tech sector due to renewed uncertainty about returns on AI-related investments hurt sentiment. Disappointing earnings updates from Amazon and Intel weighed as well.

Brent crude front-month futures rose above $114 a barrel, gaining about 3%, raising concerns about inflation and economic slowdown.

The pan European Stoxx 600 ended down 0.36%. Germany's DAX settled lower by 0.85%. France's CAC 40 ended flat, while the UK's FTSE 100 edged up 0.07%. Switzerland's SMI finished with a gain of 0.36%.

Among other markets in Europe, Austria, Czech Republic, Finland, Iceland, Ireland, Netherlands, Poland, Portugal, Spain, Sweden and Türkiye ended sharp to moderately lower.

Greece edged down marginally. Denmark, Norway and Russia closed on firm note, while Belgium ended flat.

In the UK market, Natwest Group tumbled nearly 9% after profit attributable to ordinary shareholders dropped 4.1% to 1.532 billion pounds from 1.598 billion pounds a year ago. Earnings per share were 19.1 pence, down from 19.6 pence last year.

Lloyds Group shed 5.2% and Barclays Group lost nearly 4%, while Standard Chartered drifted lower by 2.5%.

Computacenter, Polar Capital Technology Trust, Airtel Africa, Lion Finance, Scottish Mortgage, Ig Group Holdings, Rolls-Royce Holdings, Ithaca Energy, Weir Group and St. James's Place lost 3%-6%.

Endeavour Mining, Fresnillo and Antofagasta ended lower by 5.3%, 5.2% and 4.5%, respectively. Anglo American Plc shed 4.2% and Glencore ended 2.7% down, while Rio Tinto closed 1.8% down.

AstraZeneca rallied 7% after profit rose more than expected in the third quarter. The drugmaker reported that its third quarter profit attributable to owners of the Parent increased to $3.12 billion from $2.53 billion, prior year. Diluted earnings per $0.25 Ordinary Share was $2.00 compared to $1.62. GSK ended 2.2% up.

BT Group jumped 6.7%. Coca-Cola Europacific Partners climbed 3.3%. Diageo also ended 3.3% up. Relx, Reckitt Benckiser, Sainsbury (J), Unilever, Associated British Foods, Vodafone Group, Marks & Spencer, AutoTrader Group, Experian, Prudential, Tesco and British American Tobacco also moved up sharply.

BP moved modestly higher after reporting profits of $8.46 billion, well above analyst estimates, supported by strong refining margins.

In the German market, Siemens Energy shed more than 7%. Infineon lost 6.7%. Deutsche Bank, Hochtief, Siemens, Fresenius Medical Care, Continental, RWE, MTU Aero Engines, Commerzbank, Rheinmetall and Heidelberg Materials lost 1%-3.3%.

Shares of sportswear maker Puma climbed nearly 6% after gross margins improved in the third quarter. For the three-month period, the company posted a net loss of EUR 54.9 million, or EUR 0.37 per share, less than a net loss of EUR 62.3 million, or EUR 0.42 per share in the same period last year.

Bayer climbed 4.7%. Scout24, Beiersdorf, Henkel and Hannover RE gained 2%-2.5%.

Deutsche Telekom, Munich RE, Deutsche Boerse, Fresenius, SAP, Symrise, Vonovia and Adidas also closed with notable gains.

In the French market, STMicroelectronics fell 5.1%. Schneider Electric dropped 4%, while Legrand, Societe Generale, BNP Paribas, Airbus and ArcelorMittal lost 2%-3%.

Credit Agricole dropped more than 2% despite reporting higher profit for the third quarter.

Stellantis, Renault, Accor, Safran, Michelin, Thales, Bouygues and Saint-Gobain also closed weak.

Sanofi moved up 5% after clocking stronger-than-expected third-quarter earnings and lifting its FY26 outlook.

Capgemini gained 3.5% after the IT consulting group upgraded its 2026 financial targets after reporting a 12% rise in third-quarter revenue.

EssilorLuxottica, Pernod Ricard, L'Oreal, Hermes International and Air Liquide gained 2%-3.7%. Danone, Kering, Dassault Systemes and TotalEnergies also ended notably higher.

Flash data from Destatis revealed the German economy expanded more than expected in the third quarter, with Gross National Product growing 0.2% from a quarter ago, compared to the 0.3% expansion posted in the second quarter. Economists had forecast a quarterly growth of 0.1%.

On a yearly basis, calendar-adjusted GDP logged an annual growth of 1.2% after rising 1% in the preceding period. GDP was forecast to grow 1.1%.

Germany's import prices surged 10.4% year-on-year in September, accelerating from 8.3% in the previous month and exceeding market expectations of 10.3%.

Germany's seasonally adjusted unemployment rate remained unchanged at 6.4% in October, in line with market expectations and holding at its highest level since 2020.

Preliminary data from the statistical office INSEE showed France's gross domestic product fell 0.1% sequentially after stagnating in the second quarter. Economists had forecast the economy to expand 0.1%.

France's annual inflation rate rose to 3.4% in October, picking up from 3.1% in September and overshooting expectations of 3.2%, according to preliminary estimates. This marked the highest reading since December 2023.

French domestic producer prices rose 1.7% month-on-month in September, accelerating from 1% in the previous month. This marked the highest reading since March. On a yearly basis, producer prices climbed 6.8%, up from an upwardly revised 4.9% in August, marking the highest level since March 2023.

A report from Nationwide Building Society showed the UK Nationwide House Price Index rose stalled from a month earlier in October 2026, defying expectations of a 0.1% decline, and following a revised 0.3% decrease in September.

data.title: Fed Needs to Implement at Least Two More Rate Increases, Dallas Fed's Logan Says — Update
data.description:
By Jessica Coacci

The Federal Reserve needs to implement at least two more 25-basis-point rate increases given the current economic outlook after the central bank voted to hold interest rates steady this week, according to Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan.

Without any monetary-policy restraint, inflation will continue to trend above target unless unexpected shocks occur, Logan said at an event in Davidson, N.C., on Friday.

"It remains clear to me, given the current outlook, that the FOMC needs to implement at least two more 25-basis-point rate increases," Logan said. "After that, it would make sense in my view to pause and examine economic and financial developments to determine what further action may be appropriate," she added.

There had been speculation that Logan would dissent at October's Federal Open Market Committee meeting, given her previous calls for tighter monetary policy and a previous dissent she gave in July. On Friday, she offered more explanation to why she instead supported the committee's decision to hold interest rates where they are.

Financial markets have been volatile in response to news on the technology-investment outlook and geopolitical developments, she said. In such an environment, adjusting policy more gradually can help households, businesses and market participants adapt to higher rates and reduce the risk that economic activity deteriorates more sharply than necessary, she added.

Moreover, Logan said the precise timing of each rate increase has little effect on the longer-term rates most borrowers pay as long as market participants understand the FOMC's policy plans.

In addition, skipping a meeting of rate increases doesn't change the monetary-policy destination, Logan argued.

"By making the destination clear, the FOMC can better help the economy adapt and obtain the promised benefits of a skip," she explained.

Given the current outlook, the end goal should be to make policy modestly restrictive to sustainably deliver both maximum employment and stable prices, Logan said.

Write to Jessica Coacci at jessica.coacci@wsj.com
